::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** March 29th [1869]  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS British Library Add MSS 54920: 230-31
:::

My dear [Mr Macmillan](people/person_939.qmd)
I think I should enjoy editing a Globe edition of children’s books,[^1] and am much obliged to you for the proposal. I suppose the question is how many really good ones have exhausted their copy right.

Perhaps [Philip Quarl](other_books/otherbook_549.qmd) could begin the series, it is really Defoe’s but I doubt if anyone has read it.

I send 9 chapters of the [Lion](cmy_books/cmybook_81.qmd). One object is to make people think of that St Katharine’s charity, and its unhappy state of slumber. I make my heroine end there the heroine [sic] is much too poor a creature for her to marry. 

Alas! under the impression they were in type, I made away with those sheets of the [parallel history](cmy_books/cmybook_89.qmd)! I am now waiting to go to Winchester to get some large paper ruled for me.

I must try to get matters forward by August, as then the [Chaplet](cmy_books/cmybook_69.qmd) is to treat me to a trip to Paris and [Val Richer](organizations/other_205.qmd)

I am delighted with Miss Winkworth’s [number](other_books/otherbook_550.qmd) of the [Sunday Library](organizations/other_145.qmd).

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Black-edged paper.
[^2]: This project became *A Storehouse of Stories*, first series (1870) and second series (1872).
